sections.h2: Where does Branch County record deeds and mortgages?
sections.html:
Branch County records deeds and mortgages at the Register of Deeds office, 23 East Pearl Street in Coldwater, inside the Courthouse Annex. The office keeps Monday through Friday hours from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., including the lunch hour, and answers at 517-279-4320.

Paper that reaches the counter at 4:30 p.m. or later gets that day's date stamp but is recorded the following morning. The office also takes e-recordings, which helps a title company or lender closing a Coldwater, Bronson or Quincy sale from another city. Researchers can buy a monthly subscription for remote access to documents or pay for a single search.

If you only need to see what is already on record against a Branch County parcel, the county treasurer runs a free delinquent tax search at bsaonline.com. Pick Delinquent Tax Search under Online Services and look up the owner's last name, a parcel number or an address.

sections.h2: What does the Branch County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
Recording costs $30 per document no matter how many pages it runs. The county reports that $4 of each fee goes to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation fund, and that the split does not apply to fixture filings, state and federal liens, state deeds, plats or tax reversion documents. The state fee schedule behind this is MCL 600.2567.

  • Deeds, mortgages, state and federal lien notices, releases and discharges, and UCC fixture filings: $30 each.
  • A single document that assigns or discharges several instruments: $3 more for each extra instrument.
  • Copies of recorded real estate documents: $1 per page, plus $5 per document to certify a copy.
  • Name searches: 50 cents per year searched with a $5 minimum, and $3 per name for a state or federal tax lien search.
  • Fax or email delivery: $5 each.

Mail a stamped return envelope with any document you send in, or the office has no way to send the recorded original back.

sections.h2: What does a deed need before Branch County will accept it?
sections.html:
A deed must meet the format rules in MCL 565.201, and a document that misses one is returned unrecorded. The register may not turn away a compliant instrument over its content.

  • Each signer's name printed or typed beneath the signature, signed in black or dark blue ink, with the same spelling in the notary acknowledgment.
  • The notary's name printed on the same page near the notary signature.
  • A street or post office address for every grantee.
  • The name and business address of whoever drafted the document.
  • A blank top margin of at least 2 1/2 inches on page one and 1/2 inch on every other side of every page.
  • A first line that names the one recordable event the paper evidences.
  • Black ink, 10-point type or larger, white paper of 20-pound weight, cut between 8 1/2 by 11 and 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number removed, and an English translation attached to any foreign-language text.

sections.h2: Does a Branch County deed need a tax certificate first?
sections.html:
A warranty deed, any deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract, or a land contract memorandum with a warranty clause needs a tax certificate from the Branch County Treasurer before the register will record it. The rule comes from MCL 211.135, which asks for a statement that no tax liens or tax titles sit against the parcel and that taxes are paid for the five years before the date of the instrument.

The treasurer charges $5 per document for up to five property descriptions and 20 cents for each description past five. Write that fee as a separate check payable to the Treasurer's Office, apart from the $30 recording check.

A quitclaim deed with no covenants of warranty falls outside the statute, so a family transfer or a deed that cleans up a title defect usually skips the certificate. Sellers who owe back taxes should expect a warranty deed to stall until the balance is paid, which is normally handled from the sale proceeds at the title company.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does a Branch County sale cost?
sections.html:
Michigan stacks two transfer taxes on a sale. The county tax is 55 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state tax is $3.75 for each $500 under MCL 207.525. Together that is $4.30 per $500, or $8.60 per $1,000. The deed must show the total value on its face or carry a valuation affidavit.

The register collects the tax on transfers of $100 or more and posts a transfer tax schedule on its resources page. Which side pays is a matter for the purchase agreement.

Transfer tax at three Branch County prices (rates from MCL 207.504 and 207.525; $162,500 is the Census median owner-occupied value for 2020-2024)
Sale priceCounty taxState taxTotal
$100,000$110.00$750.00$860.00
$162,500$178.75$1,218.75$1,397.50
$250,000$275.00$1,875.00$2,150.00

At the county's median home value, then, the combined tax on a sale lands close to $1,400.

sections.h2: Which Branch County transfers escape transfer tax?
sections.html:
Several transfers are exempt, and the county and state lists are not identical. Both laws exempt consideration under $100, deeds given as security, leases, court-ordered transfers with no stated price, boundary-line fixes, quitclaim deeds that only confirm title, land contracts until the buyer has paid in full, and joint tenancies where one owner already held the land.

  • The state act, MCL 207.526, adds a conveyance from a person to a child, stepchild, adopted child, grandchild, step-grandchild or adopted grandchild.
  • The state act exempts any deed given in foreclosure of a mortgage or in lieu of foreclosure, while MCL 207.505 covers only loans made, guaranteed or insured by a government.
  • The county list in MCL 207.505 has no line for gifts to children, so ask the Coldwater office how it treats the county's 55 cents on a family deed.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Branch County?
sections.html:
Branch County sits in south central Michigan on the Indiana line, with Coldwater as the county seat and largest city. It was created in 1829 and organized in 1833, and at 520 square miles it is the third-smallest Michigan county by total area. Bronson is the other city, Quincy, Sherwood and Union City are villages, and sixteen townships cover the rest. The Census Bureau's 2020 count was 44,862 people, and the 2025 estimate is 45,993. Farming still anchors the local economy.

Housing here is mostly owner occupied. Census QuickFacts reports 21,287 housing units, a 77.7% owner-occupancy rate, a median owner-occupied value of $162,500, median gross rent of $959 and 16,906 households. Median household income is $63,724, 13.2% of residents live below the poverty line, and 21.1% are 65 or older. Density averages 88.6 people per square mile on 506 square miles of land.

For a seller those figures point to a modest-priced market of older homes and acreage, where the recording and transfer tax steps above matter at closing as much as the listing price does.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Branch County?
faqs.a: It costs $30 per document, whatever the page count, with $3 more for each extra instrument a single assignment or discharge covers. A warranty deed also needs a separate $5 treasurer tax certificate for up to five property descriptions.

faqs.q: Where is the Branch County Register of Deeds located?
faqs.a: The office is at 23 East Pearl Street in Coldwater, in the Courthouse Annex, and its hours are 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. The phone number is 517-279-4320.
Yes, the Register of Deeds takes e-recordings. Documents received at 4:30 p.m. or later are stamped that day and recorded the next morning, so a late submission still keeps its place in line.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate to record a quitclaim deed in Branch County?
faqs.a: Usually no. MCL 211.135 excludes a quitclaim deed or other conveyance that has no covenant of warranty from the certificate rule. A warranty deed or land contract does need one from the county treasurer.

faqs.q: Is a deed to my child taxed when I record it in Branch County?
faqs.a: The state transfer tax exempts a conveyance from a person to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild under MCL 207.526(j) and (k). The county act, MCL 207.505, lists no matching exemption, so confirm the county's 55 cents per $500 with the Register of Deeds before you record.
